hook.line: When someone asks "how was it?", "good" is not much help. *Ameno*, *pesado* and *apasionante* tell them how it felt to sit through.
hook.en: It was a very engaging talk.

examples.en: It was a very engaging talk.
That book is incredibly heavy going.
The discussion evening was very engaging.

examples.es: La película es un poco pesada, pero tiene buen final.
examples.en: The film is a bit heavy going, but it has a good ending.

examples.es: El tipo de la mesa cinco es muy pesado.
examples.en: The guy at table five is really annoying.

rule:
Three words, three feelings:
*Ameno*: easy and pleasant to follow. You never check the clock.
*Pesado*: heavy going, tedious. Said of a person, it means annoying.
*Apasionante*: gripping, a notch stronger than *ameno*.

They are adjectives, so they agree: *una charla amena, un libro pesado*. *Apasionante* has one form for both.
To go all the way, add *-ísimo*: *pesadísimo, amenísimo*. That already means "very", so skip *muy*.
Watch out: *amable* means kind, not *ameno*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a lexical cluster: a small family of words you learn together and choose between.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Fue una charla muy ___.* (*amena* or *ameno*) It was a very engaging talk.
yourTurn.why: *Charla* is feminine, so the adjective ends in *-a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Ese libro es ___.* (*pesadísimo* or *pesadísima*) That book is incredibly heavy going.
yourTurn.why: *Libro* is masculine, so the adjective ends in *-o*.
*Apasionante* has the same form for masculine and feminine.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The talk was very engaging.
yourTurn.why: *Ameno* is the word for a talk that is pleasant to follow.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: That class was incredibly heavy going.
Change the subject to a film: *Ese libro es pesadísimo.*
Make it plural: *La charla fue amena.*
yourTurn.why: Article, noun, verb and adjective all go plural.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The adjective agrees with *película*, which is feminine.
Almost. *Amable* describes kind people. For a talk that is pleasant to follow, use *amena*.

personal: Think of a book, class or show from this week. Say how it felt: *Fue… / Es…*.
